newsitem.title: USA: US Senate to vote Wednesday on Pena as Energy Secy.
newsitem.headline: US Senate to vote Wednesday on Pena as Energy Secy.

text.p: The U.S. Senate is scheduled to vote early Wednesday on the nomination of Federico Pena as Energy Secretary, Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Tuesday.
Earlier Tuesday, Minnesota Republican Sen. Rod Grams had said he would lift his objection to bringing Pena's nomination to the Senate floor.
The Senate Energy Committee last week voted 19-0 to send Pena's name to the full Senate for consideration.
The nomination of Pena, who was Transportation Secretary in President Clinton's first term, has been delayed in a standoff between the White House and some Republican senators over nuclear waste.

Grams and Senate Energy Committee Chairman Frank Murkowski, an Alaska Republican, had pressed the White House to support their bill to set up a temporary storage dump in Nevada for waste from commercial nuclear power reactors, but the White House opposes the bill.
